preamble: Spontaneous diphthongization of stressed open-mid [ɛ] (from Latin short ĕ) to a rising diphthong [jɛ]/[je] is a hallmark of Romance. Tuscan Italian and French diphthongized only in open syllables, while Spanish and Romanian did so in closed syllables as well; Portuguese and Catalan never took part, which is why Portuguese terra and pé contrast with Spanish tierra and pie.

examples.note: Tuscan diphthongization of stressed [ɛ] in open syllables.
Spanish diphthongizes stressed [ɛ] in closed syllables too; Portuguese terra keeps the monophthong.
Open-syllable diphthongization; the silent -d was added by Middle French scribes after Latin.
Romanian diphthongizes stressed [ɛ] regardless of syllable structure.

sources: Alkire, T., & Rosen, C. (2010). Romance Languages: A Historical Introduction. Cambridge University Press. https://doi.org/10.1017/CBO9780511845192
